summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video ## Making Home Goods p03: Creating Vertical Quilted Padded Headboard In this video, I will show you how to make a three-dimensional bedhead effect. Welcome to Marvelous Designer's tutorial video on how to create a three-dimensional bedhead effect. ### Opening the Previous Bedhead File First, open the previous bedhead file you made. You can also download this file from the shortcut at the bottom of this video. ### Selecting the Lines To make a three-dimensional bedhead effect, select the two lines on the front of the bedhead. In the menu bar on the right-hand side, select the line to be made according to the curve. The line to be made according to the curve will be divided into two parts. ### Creating the Bedhead Effect To create a three-dimensional bedhead effect, select the front of the bedhead and the outer part of the bedhead. Then select the new bedhead and make a joint. After making a joint, you can modify the size of the bedhead separately without affecting other bedheads. ### Freezing Layers Then, freeze the other two layers of the bedhead. Open the model and let the bedhead be divided. In order to make a three-dimensional bedhead effect, you need to stretch the outer part of the bedhead horizontally. This will provide enough volume to be opened. Stretch it again and turn on the model to check the effect. ### Adjusting Pressure for Effect Change the pressure to 10 to achieve the effect of a three-dimensional bedhead. Since the inflow effect is not very obvious, increase the pressure to 50 for a more pronounced inflow effect. ### Analyzing the Bedhead Checking the bedhead, you will see that the bedhead between the outer layer and the middle layer of the panel is biased. The bedhead between the outer layer and the middle layer of the panel is parallel to the entire circle of the panel. Therefore, the bedhead is biased only when the horizontal width is widened. ### Working with Immigrated Bedheads If you're using an immigrated bedhead, select the bedhead in the center. The width of the möbler or the width of the bedhead is equal to the width of the upper layer of the panel. ### Creating Accurate Bedhead Lines To create a more accurate bedhead, select the upper and lower edges of the upper and lower layers of the two-layer panel. Select an increase point at the intersection point in the menu to draw it in. The two lines are now in this position. These two lines will be cut off according to the internal line, which is convenient for sewing. ### Sewing the Bedhead Use the free sewing tool to sew the two sides together first. Then, use the thread sewing machine to sew the top and bottom together. After sewing, the bias of the panel line disappears, and it is sewn to the correct position. ### Creating the Effect of Straightening Next, let's create the effect of straightening. Stretch the outermost panel line. After starting the simulation, the outermost panel line is stretched by the beam, which will produce some creases. Reduce the force from 0.5 to obtain a better creasing effect. ### Conclusion See you in the next video. Bye! ```
